```sh
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"               # your runs, newest first
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"       # one run, with its score
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/feed" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"  # live: phase, status, calls, cost
```

A run's `phase` moves through `queued`, `provisioning`, `setup`, `running`, `scoring` and `done`; its `status`
ends as `scored` or `submitted` (an answer was scored), `failed` or `timed_out`. Each run carries `dataset`:
`"public"` for test runs and scored runs during the hackathon, `"private"` for the final run. On a private dataset,
`scenario_id` is left out and `error` and `answer` are `null`: they stay with the organizers.

A failed run says why in `failure_class`: `platform` (the platform failed, not your agent system: a sandbox fault, a
lost connection, our own timeout, or a hosted model down for most of the run), `agent_exit` (setup or the run exited
non-zero), `timeout`, `cancelled`, `no_answer` (it exited 0 without an answer) or `answer_rejected` (every answer it
sent was invalid); `null` while it runs and once it succeeded. A `platform` failure has `counts: false`: it counts
toward neither the ranking nor any limit, and its `error` reads "The platform failed, not your agent system. This
run doesn't count; start it again." A scored run is queued again once by itself, as the run named in `retry_run_id`
(whose `retry_of` names this one), and its `error` ends "it was started again automatically." instead.

### Cancelling a run

```sh
curl -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/cancel" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

Your team cancels its own test runs and scored runs that have not finished (organizers can cancel any run). The run
stops at once: its execution is aborted, its sandbox removed, its recording stopped and its live links revoked. It
ends as `failed` with the error `Cancelled by @you` and `finished_at` set, and your team can start the next test run
straight away. A queued run is cancelled before it starts. A cancelled scored run leaves its submission not
complete: the leaderboard ignores that submission and you can submit again. `200` returns `{"run_id", "status": "failed", "error",
"finished_at"}`; `404` means no such run of yours, `409` that it has already finished. In a browser session, send
the `x-atira-csrf` header as for every write.

### Promoting a test run

```sh
curl -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/promotion" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

A test run that handed in an eligible answer within a scored run's time limit, on the version and scenario the
public-dataset leaderboard ranks, can go on that leaderboard as it ran, without a new run. Its package becomes a
submission dated to the test run's upload, and the run becomes that submission's scored run. It goes through the
package review like any submission and counts once the review passes, usually within a couple of minutes. `201`
returns `{"run_id", "submission_id", "review": "pending"}`; `409` says why a run can't be promoted (too long, another
version or scenario, a submission of the same package still in review, the final evaluation started). The run page
has a button for it.

### Logs

Test runs and scored runs keep their output. Read it from a cursor: each page holds up to 128 chunks and the cursor
to continue from.

```sh
cursor=0
while :; do
  page=$(curl -s "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs?after=$cursor" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN")
  printf '%s' "$page" | jq -j '.chunks[].text'
  next=$(printf '%s' "$page" | jq .cursor)
  [ "$next" = "$cursor" ] && break
  cursor=$next
done
```

While the run is live, keep polling with a pause until `feed` reports `phase` `done` and its `log_cursor` is no
newer than yours. Or follow them as they arrive, as server-sent events:

```sh
curl -N "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs/stream?after=$cursor" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

Each event is one chunk: `id` is its cursor and `data` is `{"at", "stream", "text"}`. Reconnect with
`Last-Event-ID` (an `EventSource` does this by itself) or `?after=` to resume. A comment line (`: heartbeat`) comes
every 15 seconds; once the run has finished and everything is sent, an `end` event closes the stream, and connecting
again answers `204`. All of it at once, as JSON lines:

```sh
curl -o logs.jsonl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs.jsonl" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

To look at one stretch of a run, query its lines by time and content. Times are on the run's clock, as the run page
shows them: `mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss`, `3m20s` or seconds from the run's start (a minus is before it), or an ISO 8601 time.

```sh
curl -G "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs/query" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode from=02:10 --data-urlencode to=02:40 --data-urlencode stream=stdout,stderr \
  --data-urlencode 'grep=error|timeout'
```

It answers `lines` (each with `t`, its milliseconds from the start, `clock` as `mm:ss.s`, `at`, `stream` and `text`),
`matched` and `next`: up to `limit` lines (200 by default, at most 1,000), and `next` to pass as `after` while more
match. `grep` is case-insensitive text; `a|b` matches either. The `input` stream holds the clicks, scrolls and typing
the platform recorded in each browser, one line per action (`browser 1: click at 640,412`). Typed text is shown, with
keys, tokens, your run's secrets and password or one-time-code fields masked. Lines come in time order across
streams. A click, drag or drop gives its point on the browser's 1280×800 display (Chrome's bar included) and, when
the platform knew the page's geometry, the same point in the page's viewport with the viewport's size:
`browser 1: click at 200,685 (viewport 200,542 of 1279x656)`. Frames and recordings show the viewport alone, so that
point lands on a frame at 200/1279 of its width and 542/656 of its height.

`GET /v1/runs/$RUN_ID/llm-calls` lists the run's model calls in order (`at`, `provider`, `model`, `status`, tokens,
`cost_micro_usd`, `latency_ms`, and `queue_ms`, how long a call to a hosted model waited for a GPU), up to `limit`
(2,000 by default) with `next` to pass as `after`. `GET /v1/runs/$RUN_ID/screen-activity` gives, per browser, the
spans during which its screen kept changing: a gap between spans is a time the screen sat still.

Runs on the public dataset (test runs and scored runs during the hackathon) keep their logs unredacted. On a
private dataset (the final run), your logs and the feed's `error` have private values masked as `[private]`.

### Frames and recordings

```sh
curl -o frame.jpg "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/frame" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"   # the latest frame
curl -o run.webm "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"    # the recording
curl -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video/share" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"  # a link anyone can watch
curl -X DELETE "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video/share" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

A browser's screen at any time of a finished run, cut from its recording as a PNG:

```sh
curl -o at-0213.png "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/frame?t=02:13&browser=1" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

`t` takes the same times as the log query, to the nearest quarter second; outside the recording you get its first or
last frame. `X-Run-Clock` names the frame's time. Whoever may watch the recording may ask for its frames. The
platform cuts them with ffmpeg, two at a time: `429` means it is busy (retry after `Retry-After`), and `503` with
error type `frames_unavailable` means it can't right now, so cut the frame yourself from `video/source` (`ffmpeg -ss
133 -i "<url>" -frames:v 1 frame.png`; `atira mcp` does this for you when ffmpeg is installed).

`frame` without `t` answers `204` until there is a frame, and `304` for an unchanged one sent with `If-None-Match`. `video` serves
byte ranges. `video/source` tells a player where to read the recording: a presigned URL straight to storage
(`direct: true`, plays in a `<video>`, works until `expires_at`, `expires_in` seconds from now, at most 10 minutes;
ask again after that), or else `video` itself. A recording kept as HLS (`hls: true`, most recent runs) is a
playlist: `url` is `video/hls/index.m3u8` on this API, each segment from it too
(hls.js plays it, and `ffmpeg -headers "x-api-key: …" -i <url>` reads it); `native_url` names presigned segments
instead, for a player's own HLS; `video` then answers `303` to the run's page. `videos` places a run's recordings on its timeline, as the run page replays them: each browser's first
frame time (`started_at`, epoch ms) and length, `estimated` when the start time is approximate. Your team
sees the frames and recordings of its runs on the public dataset, test runs and scored runs alike; a private dataset's
(the final run's) stay with the organizers unless they release them.

A run whose `agent.json` asks for several browsers has a frame and a recording per browser: add `?browser=n`
(1 to 4; browser 1 without it), for example `/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/frame?browser=2` or `/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video?browser=3`.
`feed` then carries `browsers` and `frames` (each browser's `frame_at` and `frame_hash`), the run lists its
recordings in `videos`, and a share link's response adds `urls`, one per recording. A browser the run does not have
answers `404`; a value other than 1 to 4 answers `400`.

### Live screen and terminal

Where available, your team can watch the screen of a run on the public dataset (a test run or a
scored run) live while its agent runs, and a test run's terminal. The run page shows the screens beside the live
logs; an agent or script can ask for the view-only links itself:


lost connection, our own timeout, or a hosted model down for most of the run), `agent_exit` (setup or the run exited
non-zero), `timeout`, `cancelled`, `no_answer` (it exited 0 without an answer) or `answer_rejected` (every answer it
sent was invalid); `null` while it runs and once it succeeded. A `platform` failure has `counts: false`: it counts
toward neither the ranking nor any limit, and its `error` reads "The platform failed, not your agent system. This
run doesn't count; start it again." A scored run is queued again once by itself, as the run named in `retry_run_id`
(whose `retry_of` names this one), and its `error` ends "it was started again automatically." instead.

```sh

```

Your team cancels its own test runs and scored runs that have not finished (organizers can cancel any run). The run
stops at once: its execution is aborted, its sandbox removed, its recording stopped and its live links revoked. It
ends as `failed` with the error `Cancelled by @you` and `finished_at` set, and your team can start the next test run
straight away. A queued run is cancelled before it starts. A cancelled scored run leaves its submission not
complete: the leaderboard ignores that submission and you can submit again. `200` returns `{"run_id", "status": "failed", "error",
"finished_at"}`; `404` means no such run of yours, `409` that it has already finished. In a browser session, send
the `x-atira-csrf` header as for every write.

public-dataset leaderboard ranks, can go on that leaderboard as it ran, without a new run. Its package becomes a

### Logs

Test runs and scored runs keep their output. Read it from a cursor: each page holds up to 128 chunks and the cursor
to continue from.

```sh
cursor=0
while :; do
  page=$(curl -s "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs?after=$cursor" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN")
  printf '%s' "$page" | jq -j '.chunks[].text'
  next=$(printf '%s' "$page" | jq .cursor)
  [ "$next" = "$cursor" ] && break

done
```

While the run is live, keep polling with a pause until `feed` reports `phase` `done` and its `log_cursor` is no
newer than yours. Or follow them as they arrive, as server-sent events:

```sh

```

`Last-Event-ID` (an `EventSource` does this by itself) or `?after=` to resume. A comment line (`: heartbeat`) comes
every 15 seconds; once the run has finished and everything is sent, an `end` event closes the stream, and connecting
again answers `204`. All of it at once, as JSON lines:

```sh

```

To look at one stretch of a run, query its lines by time and content. Times are on the run's clock, as the run page
shows them: `mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss`, `3m20s` or seconds from the run's start (a minus is before it), or an ISO 8601 time.

```sh

  --data-urlencode 'grep=error|timeout'
```

`matched` and `next`: up to `limit` lines (200 by default, at most 1,000), and `next` to pass as `after` while more
match. `grep` is case-insensitive text; `a|b` matches either. The `input` stream holds the clicks, scrolls and typing
the platform recorded in each browser, one line per action (`browser 1: click at 640,412`). Typed text is shown, with
keys, tokens, your run's secrets and password or one-time-code fields masked. Lines come in time order across
streams. A click, drag or drop gives its point on the browser's 1280×800 display (Chrome's bar included) and, when
the platform knew the page's geometry, the same point in the page's viewport with the viewport's size:
`browser 1: click at 200,685 (viewport 200,542 of 1279x656)`. Frames and recordings show the viewport alone, so that
point lands on a frame at 200/1279 of its width and 542/656 of its height.

`GET /v1/runs/$RUN_ID/llm-calls` lists the run's model calls in order (`at`, `provider`, `model`, `status`, tokens,

spans during which its screen kept changing: a gap between spans is a time the screen sat still.

private dataset (the final run), your logs and the feed's `error` have private values masked as `[private]`.

class BidFlow:
    """
    The bid form overlapped with the research. Right after the briefing, a worker (the model) does the form's steps
    that need no calculated value (bidder data with the contact address, expression of interest, the main offer as
    offer type) and maps the controls of the first position page, then stops there. While the research runs, a
    cheap background request keeps the portal session (and with it the unsaved wizard state) alive; when the
    session is lost anyway, the page is reloaded and the steps are done again. finish() then enters the answer from
    the position step on, checks and signs (submit_bid). If the research ends in no_bid, a short pass goes back
    to the offer type, which clears only empty steps. AGENT_FORM_OVERLAP=0 turns this off.
    """

    def __init__(self, session: SiteSession, mailbox: Mailbox, briefing: Briefing, deadline: float):
        self.session, self.mailbox, self.briefing, self.deadline = session, mailbox, briefing, deadline
        self.desk = PositionDesk({}, deadline)
        self.address: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self.task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self.ready = False  # a pass stopped at the positions and the session has not been lost since
        self.preparing = False
        self.passes = 0
        self.rewound = False  # a no-bid went back from the positions to the offer-type step
        self.desk.plan.decimal = decimal_mark(briefing.submission_steps)

    def start(self) -> None:
        self.address = asyncio.create_task(self.mailbox.address())
        if os.environ.get("AGENT_FORM_OVERLAP", "1") != "0":
            self.task = asyncio.create_task(self._run())

    def contact_address(self) -> asyncio.Task:
        """The address lookup; started again when the first one found nothing (e.g. the webmail was still down)."""
        if self.address is None or (self.address.done() and (self.address.cancelled() or not self.address.result())):
            self.address = asyncio.create_task(self.mailbox.address())
        return self.address

    def _event(self, kind: str, **data) -> None:
        self.session.trace.event("bid_flow", kind, **data)

    async def _run(self) -> None:
        while self.passes < PREPARES and self.deadline - time.monotonic() > SIGNING_RESERVE + 300:
            try:
                await self._prepare()
                if not self.ready:
                    return
                await self._keep_alive()  # returns only when the session was lost
                async with self.session.lock:  # sign in again and show where the wizard stands now
                    await self.session._goto(self.session.page.url)
            except Exception as error:  # e.g. a model error: another pass; at worst the form starts from scratch
                self.preparing = self.ready = False
                self._event("failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:300]}")
                await asyncio.sleep(5)
        self.preparing = False

    async def _prepare(self) -> None:
        self.passes += 1
        self.preparing, self.ready = True, False
        started = time.monotonic()
        address = self.contact_address()

        async def bidder_contact_email(reason: str = "") -> str:
            """The bidder's contact email address, read from the bidder's own webmail."""
            found = await address
            self.session.seen += "\n" + found
            return found or "not found: the webmail did not show it"

        b = self.briefing
        goal = f"""Prepare the bid for tender {b.tender_reference} on this website while its values are still being
calculated. Follow the brief's submission steps below, but only those that need no calculated value: express
interest if the website asks for it, open the bid submission, register the bidder with company name
{b.company_name!r}, VAT id {b.vat_id!r} and the contact email from bidder_contact_email(), and choose the main offer
as the offer type (not an alternative offer, not a declaration that you do not bid). Save each of these steps
with the form's next/continue button. Do not open documents, questions or other pages.
Stop at the first step that asks for position values (materials, quantities, prices, lead times), the discount or
the total: enter, choose, omit, add or save nothing there. If that step shows one position, call
map_position_form() once with {mapping_guide(VALUE_NAMES)}
Then return. Refs change with every view: read a button's label in the latest view before clicking it.

Brief's submission steps:
{b.submission_steps}"""
        tools = (bidder_contact_email, self.desk.map_position_form, fill_in)
        until = min(started + PREPARE_SECONDS, self.deadline - SIGNING_RESERVE - 240)
        result, _ = await run_worker(self.session, goal, PrepareResult, deadline=until, max_steps=20, notes=False,
                                     grounded=False,
                                     thinking=llm.thinking("form", False), tools=tools)
        self.ready = bool(result and result.at_positions)
        self.preparing = False
        self._event("prepared", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1), at_positions=self.ready,
                    step=result.step if result else None, mapped=bool(self.desk.plan.fields), passes=self.passes)

    async def _keep_alive(self) -> None:
        """A light request to the website every KEEPALIVE_SECONDS; returns once the session is found signed out."""
        while True:
            await asyncio.sleep(KEEPALIVE_SECONDS)
            try:  # from inside the page: the sandbox resolves the websites only in the browser, not in this process
                url, body = await asyncio.wait_for(self.session.page.evaluate(KEEPALIVE_JS), 20)
            except Exception as error:  # a slow website: try again next time
                self._event("keepalive_failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
                continue
            if SIGNED_OUT.search(body):
                self.ready = False
                self._event("session_lost", url=url)
                return

    async def rewind(self) -> bool:
        """
        A no-bid after the early pass chose the main offer: one short pass goes back to the offer-type step (the
        steps in between hold nothing yet), so the form pass starts where the declaration is chosen. When it does
        not get there, the form pass is told to go back itself (the `prepared` hint of _positions).
        """
        started = time.monotonic()
        goal = f"""The bid for tender {self.briefing.tender_reference} is a no-bid after all. An earlier pass chose the
main offer and went on to a later step of this form. Go back to the step where the offer type is chosen (main
offer, alternative offer or the declaration not to bid) with the form's own back/previous button or its step
navigation, one step at a time, without entering, choosing or saving anything on the way. Return as soon as the
offer-type step shows; do not choose anything there. Refs change with every view: read a button's label in the
latest view before clicking it."""
        until = min(started + REWIND_SECONDS, self.deadline - SIGNING_RESERVE - 60)
        try:
            result, _ = await run_worker(self.session, goal, OfferTypeStep, deadline=until, max_steps=REWIND_STEPS,
                                         notes=False, grounded=False, thinking=llm.thinking("form", False))
        except Exception as error:
            self._event("rewind_failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")
            result = None
        self.rewound = bool(result and result.at_offer_type)
        self._event("rewound", ok=self.rewound, step=result.step if result else None,
                    seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1))
        return self.rewound

    async def finish(self, answer: dict | None, attributes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None
                     ) -> SubmissionResult | None:
        """Enter the research's answer from where the form stands, check and sign."""
        if self.task is not None:
            waited = time.monotonic()
            while self.preparing and time.monotonic() - waited < FINISH_WAIT:  # a pass is still on the form
                await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
            self.task.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(self.task, return_exceptions=True)
            self._event("handover", ready=self.ready, waited=round(time.monotonic() - waited, 1))
        if self.ready and answer and answer.get("decision") == "no_bid":
            await self.rewind()
        return await submit_bid(self.session, self.mailbox, self.briefing, self.deadline, answer, attributes,
                                flow=self)

        self.address = asyncio.create_task(self.mailbox.address())
        if os.environ.get("AGENT_FORM_OVERLAP", "1") != "0":
            self.task = asyncio.create_task(self._run())

    def contact_address(self) -> asyncio.Task:
        """The address lookup; started again when the first one found nothing (e.g. the webmail was still down)."""
        if self.address is None or (self.address.done() and (self.address.cancelled() or not self.address.result())):
            self.address = asyncio.create_task(self.mailbox.address())
        return self.address

    def _event(self, kind: str, **data) -> None:
        self.session.trace.event("bid_flow", kind, **data)

    async def _run(self) -> None:
        while self.passes < PREPARES and self.deadline - time.monotonic() > SIGNING_RESERVE + 300:
            try:
                await self._prepare()
                if not self.ready:
                    return
                await self._keep_alive()  # returns only when the session was lost
                async with self.session.lock:  # sign in again and show where the wizard stands now
                    await self.session._goto(self.session.page.url)
            except Exception as error:  # e.g. a model error: another pass; at worst the form starts from scratch
                self.preparing = self.ready = False
                self._event("failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:300]}")
                await asyncio.sleep(5)
        self.preparing = False

    async def _prepare(self) -> None:
        self.passes += 1
        self.preparing, self.ready = True, False
        started = time.monotonic()
        address = self.contact_address()

        async def bidder_contact_email(reason: str = "") -> str:
            """The bidder's contact email address, read from the bidder's own webmail."""
            found = await address
            self.session.seen += "\n" + found
            return found or "not found: the webmail did not show it"

        b = self.briefing
        goal = f"""Prepare the bid for tender {b.tender_reference} on this website while its values are still being
calculated. Follow the brief's submission steps below, but only those that need no calculated value: express
interest if the website asks for it, open the bid submission, register the bidder with company name
{b.company_name!r}, VAT id {b.vat_id!r} and the contact email from bidder_contact_email(), and choose the main offer
as the offer type (not an alternative offer, not a declaration that you do not bid). Save each of these steps
with the form's next/continue button. Do not open documents, questions or other pages.
Stop at the first step that asks for position values (materials, quantities, prices, lead times), the discount or
the total: enter, choose, omit, add or save nothing there. If that step shows one position, call
map_position_form() once with {mapping_guide(VALUE_NAMES)}
Then return. Refs change with every view: read a button's label in the latest view before clicking it.

Brief's submission steps:
{b.submission_steps}"""
        tools = (bidder_contact_email, self.desk.map_position_form, fill_in)
        until = min(started + PREPARE_SECONDS, self.deadline - SIGNING_RESERVE - 240)
        result, _ = await run_worker(self.session, goal, PrepareResult, deadline=until, max_steps=20, notes=False,
                                     grounded=False,
                                     thinking=llm.thinking("form", False), tools=tools)
        self.ready = bool(result and result.at_positions)
        self.preparing = False
        self._event("prepared", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1), at_positions=self.ready,
                    step=result.step if result else None, mapped=bool(self.desk.plan.fields), passes=self.passes)

    async def _keep_alive(self) -> None:
        """A light request to the website every KEEPALIVE_SECONDS; returns once the session is found signed out."""
        while True:
            await asyncio.sleep(KEEPALIVE_SECONDS)
            try:  # from inside the page: the sandbox resolves the websites only in the browser, not in this process
                url, body = await asyncio.wait_for(self.session.page.evaluate(KEEPALIVE_JS), 20)
            except Exception as error:  # a slow website: try again next time
                self._event("keepalive_failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
                continue
            if SIGNED_OUT.search(body):
                self.ready = False
                self._event("session_lost", url=url)
                return

    async def rewind(self) -> bool:
        """
        A no-bid after the early pass chose the main offer: one short pass goes back to the offer-type step (the
        steps in between hold nothing yet), so the form pass starts where the declaration is chosen. When it does
        not get there, the form pass is told to go back itself (the `prepared` hint of _positions).
        """
        started = time.monotonic()
        goal = f"""The bid for tender {self.briefing.tender_reference} is a no-bid after all. An earlier pass chose the
main offer and went on to a later step of this form. Go back to the step where the offer type is chosen (main
offer, alternative offer or the declaration not to bid) with the form's own back/previous button or its step
navigation, one step at a time, without entering, choosing or saving anything on the way. Return as soon as the
offer-type step shows; do not choose anything there. Refs change with every view: read a button's label in the
latest view before clicking it."""
        until = min(started + REWIND_SECONDS, self.deadline - SIGNING_RESERVE - 60)
        try:
            result, _ = await run_worker(self.session, goal, OfferTypeStep, deadline=until, max_steps=REWIND_STEPS,
                                         notes=False, grounded=False, thinking=llm.thinking("form", False))
        except Exception as error:
            self._event("rewind_failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")
            result = None
        self.rewound = bool(result and result.at_offer_type)
        self._event("rewound", ok=self.rewound, step=result.step if result else None,
                    seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1))
        return self.rewound

    async def finish(self, answer: dict | None, attributes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None
                     ) -> SubmissionResult | None:
        """Enter the research's answer from where the form stands, check and sign."""
        if self.task is not None:
            waited = time.monotonic()
            while self.preparing and time.monotonic() - waited < FINISH_WAIT:  # a pass is still on the form
                await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
            self.task.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(self.task, return_exceptions=True)
            self._event("handover", ready=self.ready, waited=round(time.monotonic() - waited, 1))
        if self.ready and answer and answer.get("decision") == "no_bid":
            await self.rewind()
        return await submit_bid(self.session, self.mailbox, self.briefing, self.deadline, answer, attributes,
                                flow=self)

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages
entries.description: Read browser console messages (console.log, console.error, console.warn, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging JavaScript errors, viewing application logs, or understanding what's happening in the browser console. Returns console messages from the current domain only. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs. IMPORTANT: Always provide a pattern to filter messages - without a pattern, you may get too many irrelevant messages.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read console messages from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

onlyErrors.description: If true, only return error and exception messages. Default is false (return all message types).

clear.description: If true, clear the console messages after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to filter console messages. Only messages matching this pattern will be returned (e.g., 'error|warning' to find errors and warnings, 'MyApp' to filter app-specific logs). You should always provide a pattern to avoid getting too many irrelevant messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__resize_window
entries.description: Resize the current browser window to specified dimensions. Useful for testing responsive designs or setting up specific screen sizes. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to get the window for. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__browser_batch
entries.description: Execute a sequence of browser tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — if an action navigates to a domain without permission, the next item's check fails and the batch stops. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested.

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, tabs_create_mcp). browser_batch cannot be nested.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","coordinate":[100,200],"tabId":123}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello","tabId":123}},{"name":"navigate","input":{"url":"https://example.com","tabId":123}}]

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

content.text:
The dashboard now has a live pipeline section, working in a local preview at http://127.0.0.1:3123 (still running). It is not committed and not deployed to the public Vercel link yet.

I checked it against real runs, one in flight and one finished, by rendering the page in headless Chromium, and the 18 tests pass. The Chrome extension is connected to a different machine and could not reach my localhost.

## What it shows

- **Pipeline:** six columns of step cards joined by lines, in the style of your photo: Start, Understand, Read, Match, Decide, Bid. The steps run from sandbox and site sign-ins through brief, plan, the parallel readers, ERP, verify, gaps and calc to the bid form, TAN, signing and score.
- **Live state:** running steps get a dark border, a pulsing dot, a running timer and the number of tabs at work. The line feeding a running step animates.
- **What the run holds so far:** a table of counts for requirements, tender positions, Q&A amendments, ERP records, mail records, chosen materials, verified facts, gaps, problems, refused values and the answer.
- **Happening now:** a newest-first line per event, such as "Verifier checked 33 facts" or "TAN found in the mailbox".
- **Run picker:** it follows the newest live run by itself; you can pin any run, and each run row in the builds table has a "pipeline" link to view that run.

## Things you should know

- **Counts only, no site values.** The link is public and the run logs contain tender references, material numbers and prices. The server reduces each log line to step, counts, flags and timings before anything reaches the browser. So "what we are storing" is shown as how many of each thing, not the contents. I checked the real output for leaks and found none.
- **Late viewers miss early steps.** The platform keeps only a run's newest ~260 output lines, even while it runs. A page that stays open accumulates everything; one opened mid-run shows earlier steps as dashed "before this page was watching". Finished runs are mostly filled in from the summary the agent prints at the end.
- **Main is merged in.** I merged `origin/main` into `monitoring` (merge commit `9f05522`), keeping both sides of the two conflicts in `.gitignore` and `docs/learned.md`. Nothing is pushed, and `origin/monitoring` still has six stage-dashboard commits this branch lacks.
- **One small fix to existing code:** the page's clock could show "01:60"; it now rounds correctly.

The new code is in `monitor/api/pipeline.js`, `monitor/api/_pipeline.js` and `monitor/pipeline.js`, with the page changes in `monitor/index.html`.

Do you want me to commit this and deploy it to the Vercel link? Deploying makes the pipeline view visible to anyone with the URL.
